title: Contoso Support Copilot
body:
Contoso is building a support copilot that answers customer questions from a corpus of about four million product documents.

Current architecture
• Documents land in Azure Blob Storage as PDFs, uploaded continuously by a content team.
• A Python worker chunks each document, calls Azure OpenAI for embeddings, and writes chunks plus vectors to a store.
• A front-end API retrieves the closest chunks for a question and passes them to a chat model.
• Everything runs in Azure Container Apps in a single region.

Requirements
• Ingestion must survive a multi-hour outage of the embedding worker without losing documents.
• Retrieval must be filtered to the customer's own tenant, and tenants vary from 50 to 400,000 chunks.
• The p95 retrieval latency budget is 150 ms.
• The embedding worker must cost nothing when no documents are waiting.
• Support engineers must be able to trace one customer question end to end across the API, retrieval and the model call.

Constraints
• No secrets may be stored in application configuration.
• The team has no Kubernetes experience and wants to keep it that way.

title: Fabrikam ingestion rebuild
body:
Fabrikam runs a nightly batch that re-embeds its entire catalogue. The job currently runs as a single Azure Function on the Consumption plan and has started failing.

Symptoms
• The function is terminated part-way through, always at roughly the same elapsed time.
• Cosmos DB returns HTTP 429 in bursts during the run, concentrated on the largest publisher.
• A downstream search index still lists products that were deleted from Cosmos DB weeks ago.
• Application Insights shows the ingestion worker as a separate operation from the API that triggers it.

Requirements
• The nightly job must complete in one run and must not keep a replica alive between runs.
• Deleted products must disappear from the search index within an hour.
• The team wants to keep the existing Cosmos DB account and partition key if at all possible.
